newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev firms despite rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev firms despite rate cut.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev opened at 1,430-1,440 per dollar, up from Thursday's close at 1,435-1,445 despite the longer value date of spot deals and a cut in the main interest rate, dealers said.
"Dollar supply heavily tops demand and pushes the lev up despite the rate cut and and the longer than usual value date," a commercial bank dealer said.
Dealers said demand for government securities from domestic and foreign players was behind increased dollar supply.
The value date of today's spot deals is May 5 because markets will be closed from Monday through Thursday for Eastern Orthodox Easter.

The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) on Thursday cut its main interest rate to 6.20 percent monthly from 8.03 percent in line with the falling yield on short-term government securities. The new interest rate is effective on Monday, April 28.

Local and foreign investors, attracted by high yields and pending privatisation sell-offs, kept selling foreign currency for levs to buy government securities, dealers said. They also said investors were encouraged by the recent lev rise. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
